blocks.content: Course: Make Your Website Interactive with JavaScript
The slider moves. The buttons respond. But right now nothing stops the user from clicking Prev on the first slide or Next on the last.
That is an invalid state. And it needs to be handled.

items: On the first slide, Prev should be disabled. There is nowhere to go back.
On the last slide, Next should be disabled. There is nowhere to go forward.

blocks.content: This prevents an invalid state and gives clear feedback.
Use the current index (for example, currentSlideIndex) to decide:

items: If the index is 0, disable Prev
If the index is the last slide, disable Next

blocks.content: You can update the buttons in two ways:

items: Set button.disabled = true or false in JavaScript
Or toggle a class and style the disabled state in CSS

blocks.content: Update this every time the slide changes, so the buttons always match the current position.
Update the disabled state inside showSlide(). That way, every change goes through one function, and the buttons never fall out of sync.
Next, you will see a runnable example where the buttons disable automatically at the first and last slide.
